861-major-in-environment-b-sc: Science B.Sc. students have two extra concentrations: Atmospheric Environment and Air Quality, and Earth Sciences and Economics. All take 21 core ENVR credits.
861-location: Downtown: 3534 University St., H3A 2A7, 514-398-2827. Macdonald: Rowles House, 21,111 Lakeshore Rd., Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, H9X 3V9.
861-program-description: Pollution problems from urban smog to global effects. Covers how air moves pollutants, up to the stratosphere or trapped near the ground, how rain removes them, atmospheric chemistry, and measuring what's in the air.
862-analytical-chemistry-calculus: CHEM 267 or FDSC 213: no credit for both.
862-math-or-physical-science: 9 credits, 6 at 300+. Only one each of ATOC 519 or CHEM 519, AEMA 305 or MATH 315.
863-program-description: Resources come from the Earth and return as waste. Geology governs both, and economics shapes energy choices and waste treatment. You learn minerals, rocks, soils, waters and their interactions, plus economic theory and policy on resources, waste and warming.
864-natural-resources: Only one each of ANTH 451 or GEOG 451, BIOL 451 or NRSC 451, ENVB 529 or GEOG 201.
865-honours-program-in-environment: For B.Sc. and B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) Majors, the B.A. Faculty Program and the B.A. & Sc. Interfaculty Program. A 6-credit, two-term supervised research project in your final year, good preparation for graduate school, with no extra time. If you can't finish Honours you can still graduate in the regular program.
865-program-description-2: For the B.A. Faculty Program only. Apply in March of U2, seeing the Program Adviser. Enter with a Program GPA of 3.3; earn at least B in ENVR 495D1/D2; graduate with CGPA 3.0 and Program GPA 3.3. Also complete a minor concentration outside the School.
54 credits of core and domain plus 6 of Honours. Present at the Honours Symposium and give your report to the Adviser.
866-program-description: For the B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) Major only. Apply in March of U2. Enter with a Program GPA of 3.3; earn at least B in ENVR 495D1/D2; graduate with CGPA 3.0 and Program GPA 3.3.
60–63 credits of core and domain plus 6 of Honours. Present at the Honours Symposium and give your report to the Adviser.
866-honours-required-courses-6-credits-2: ENVR 495D1/D2 over consecutive terms, or 495N1/N2 over non-consecutive terms.
868-joint-honours-component-environment: Taken with a second B.A. Joint Honours Component (p. 160): a two-term interdisciplinary final-year research project under supervision.
868-program-description: Combines Honours in any two Arts disciplines. See an adviser in each department about courses and research. Enter at the end of U1 and keep a Program GPA of 3.30 and CGPA of 3.0. Unlike the Faculty Program Honours, no Minor is needed.
868-program-prerequisites-or-corequisite: 6–8 credits on top of the program, done by the end of U1: 3 of basic science (or CEGEP Biology 00UK, Chemistry 00UL, Physics 00UR) and one more, such as 3 of calculus (or CEGEP 00UN).
868-honours-research: 6 research credits across both components. If your other component requires 0, 3 or 6, take 6, 3 or 0 of ENVR. The same credits can't count twice.
6–12 more credits chosen with the Adviser, at most 3 at 200–300 level.
870-diploma-in-environment: Adds undergraduate Environment coursework to a finished degree. 30 credits at McGill, one year full-time. For B.Sc. or B.A. holders in good standing, through whichever of the three faculties fits your background. The Program Advisor approves courses.
870-complementary-courses-12-credits: With the Advisor's approval: 3 credits outside your first degree's area (Natural Sciences and Technology after a B.A., Social Sciences and Policy after a B.Sc.), and 9 in one focus, 6 of them at 400+.
871-natural-sciences-and-technology: Only one of each: LSCI 230 or MIMM 211; ENVB 529 or GEOG 201; BREE 217, CIVE 323 or GEOG 322; BIOL 308 or ENVB 305; BIOL 465 or WILD 421; COMP 202 or COMP 204; EPSC 201 or EPSC 233.
873-faculty-of-law: Trains jurists across languages, jurisdictions, legal traditions, disciplines and cultures. The double degree compares legal traditions and increasingly includes Indigenous ones, in line with the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's calls to action, on Kanien'kehá:ka territory. Teaching is in English and French, in civil and common law, in francophone Montreal.

Professors come from around the world. The 2019 entering class had students born in 29 countries with 15 mother tongues; graduate students come from five continents. The Faculty is working to welcome more kinds of learners, and to better represent Canadian society and Indigenous peoples.
873-legal-education-at-mcgill: Bilingual and pluralistic, so your understanding of law isn't tied to one jurisdiction or tradition.
Integrated first-year coursework in French and English, built on civil and common law, plus Indigenous law and alternate dispute resolution.

Small groups work on legal method, ethics, empirical research and policy. One-week intensives on special topics run in fall and winter. Modern classrooms, with students leading more of their own learning.
873-location: Faculty of Law: Chancellor Day Hall, 3644 Peel St., H3A 1W9, 514-398-6666, mcgill.ca/law.
Undergraduate Admissions: New Chancellor Day Hall, Room 418, 514-398-6602, admissions.law@mcgill.ca.
873-admissions-policy: Reviewers look at the whole application: academic record, languages, motivation, activities and references, plus substantial reading and listening in both English and French. They look for curiosity, engagement, insight, leadership, teamwork, openness, maturity and ethics. No GPA or LSAT cut-offs, and no quotas.
Applications are especially welcome from Indigenous peoples, people with disabilities, racialized people, 2SLGBTQ+ people, women, people from disadvantaged backgrounds, and others facing barriers.

Limited and competitive: about 180 admitted each year, with about eight applicants per place, so many qualified people are refused. The Admissions Office and a committee of professors, senior law students and two Assistant Deans review files.
874-educational-requirements: You need at least 60 university credits, a Quebec DCS, or a Quebec French Baccalaureate (Collège international Marie de France or Collège Stanislas). Not eligible: French Baccalaureate from outside Quebec, IB, or high school students.
Almost everyone admitted as a University applicant has finished a degree. No minimum GPA, LSAT or R-score, though admitted students tend to have outstanding records; the website has statistics.
If you enter from CEGEP or the Quebec Baccalaureate and want to practise in the US, some state bars require university study before law.
874-language-requirements: You must be at least passively bilingual: C1 in one of English or French and B2 reading and listening in the other (CEFR). This is a minimum, not an advantage.

You may write and speak in either language, regardless of the course's language, and do Moot Court in either. First-year courses run in both; some upper-year ones in one only. Exam questions follow the course language but can include long passages in either. Nearly all first-years get at least one French section.

Say how you learned both languages and include language course transcripts, or you'll be refused. Supreme Court of Canada judgments show the reading level expected. If you plan on the Barreau or Chambre des notaires, see the Charter of the French Language requirements (p. 70).
874-indigenous-applicants: First Nations (Status and Non-Status), Inuit, Métis and other Indigenous persons with ties to Turtle Island are encouraged to apply and to self-identify, which helps McGill share services and funding and track recruitment. You may choose another category instead, following its rules.
875-linguistic-support: Don't rule yourself out over language, as English or French may be a third language or feel colonial; talk to the Faculty. The McCarthy Tétrault Fund for Language Training pays for language work before and during the program.
875-indigenous-student-financial-assista: A McGill funding program, supported in part by Indspire, an Indigenous-led charity.
875-indigenous-research-and-experiential: Research with scholars in both languages; the Indigenous Law Association; Indigenous Human Rights Initiatives; the Legal Clinic at Kahnawà:ke; L.E.X. with the Kahnawà:ke Survival School; the Kawaskimhon Moot; and a Minor in Indigenous Studies.

Terms away at the University of Arizona's Indigenous Peoples Law and Policy Program or Osgoode Hall's Intensive Program in Indigenous Lands, Resources and Governments. In 2022, a pilot month-long Anishinaabe Law Field School with Manitoba's Treaty Relations Commission. Several funding sources may apply.
875-first-peoples-house: A home away from home: community, mentoring, computers, guest lectures, elder visits, academic counselling, a resource centre and housing.
875-indigenous-law-centre-programming: The University of Saskatchewan's centre works on access to legal education, law that better serves Indigenous communities, and sharing information. Incoming Indigenous students are encouraged to look into it first.
875-honesty-and-integrity-of-applicants: False, incomplete, inconsistent or misleading information is misconduct, whether intended or not. Examples include a personal statement you didn't write, or not disclosing an LSAT score. McGill may refuse you or withdraw an offer, and may report you to LSAC.
875-application-process-for-b-c-l-j-d-de: Apply early, with all documents in by the deadline. Only complete files get reviewed.
875-online-application: Online from September 1. Email the Law Admissions Office if you can't apply online (transfer applicants). You should get an acknowledgement within 48 hours; if not, contact them.
876-verifying-the-status-of-your-applica: Watching the Applicant Portal is your job. "Provide supporting documents" means incomplete, and incomplete files are cancelled after the deadline, except when only an LSAT score is missing ("Items outstanding"). "In review" lasts until a decision.

Near deadlines documents can take 48 hours to show up, so contact the office only if your file is still incomplete 48 hours after the deadline. Upload documents through the Portal once you have your acknowledgement.
876-review-of-applications: Complete files are assessed against the Admissions Policy and compared with other applicants.
876-admission-decisions: You get an email and the decision in the Portal, never by phone. Review can run into June, and waitlist decisions until the end of August.
876-application-fee: Non-refundable; see Student Accounts for the amount. Requires Visa, MasterCard or American Express, processed through Moneris, and not stored by McGill.
876-applicant-categories: Leading to the degree, September only: University, Mature, CEGEP and Quebec French Baccalaureate, Advanced Standing, Transfer.
Not leading to a degree, September or January: Visiting, Incoming Exchange, Comité des équivalences, Special.
876-university-applicants: On track to finish a degree, or with at least 60 undergraduate credits; includes those with over 30 credits beyond a DCS by registration. With 60 credits you may apply, but admission is unlikely unless you'll finish your degree first.
876-mature-applicants: Five or more years away from formal education, not necessarily in a row. You're placed here automatically from your academic history. Same criteria and educational requirements, no set number admitted, and with close attention to professional activities. An interview may be needed.
876-cegep-and-quebec-french-baccalaureat: With a DCS or Quebec French Baccalaureate, and up to 30 university credits by registration. Only Collèges Marie de France and Stanislas qualify; a French Baccalaureate or IB from outside Quebec needs 60 full-time university credits first.
Not eligible for joint degrees. Potentially admissible candidates must attend an interview. US practice may require university study before law.
877-advanced-standing-students: For holders of a recognized law degree, typically one allowing a bar exam or graduate law in that jurisdiction, unless using the Comité des équivalences. French applicants need a licence en droit, not a DEUG. Few places; same criteria, with emphasis on your law grades.

Earn at least 75 McGill credits and the integrated B.C.L./J.D.; neither degree stands alone. Usually you take Property, Contractual Obligations and Extra-Contractual Obligations/Torts. The Associate Dean (Academic) sets equivalences.
877-transfer-students: After at least a full-time year at another Canadian law faculty. Few places; same criteria, with emphasis on law grades and your reasons. At least 75 McGill credits, about 2.5 years. Usually you retake the private law courses, with no credit for property, obligations, contracts or torts from your first year.

Send Winter results as soon as you have them; they are needed for evaluation. A law certificate doesn't qualify or count, and you need Good Standing. Online until November 1, deadline May 1; afterwards ask for a paper form.
877-comite-des-equivalences: For holders of a recognized law degree meeting Barreau du Québec or Chambre des notaires requirements. Submit your equivalency application before the document deadline, and have the final decision by registration. Non-degree, with no credit toward a McGill law degree; not for National Committee on Accreditation requirements.
877-visiting-students-letters-of-permiss: After two years at another law faculty, in Good Standing, spend a term here if space permits. Apply through Admissions with a Letter of Permission. The Director (Student Life and Learning) decides and arranges your courses. Non-degree.
878-incoming-exchange-students: From law programs with a McGill exchange agreement or through BCI. Your home university nominates you and has its own deadlines. Apply online with no fee; generally a B average minimum. The Director decides and it's final. Limited places, with no guarantee of restricted courses. Non-degree.
878-special-students: Exceptional and limited, for compelling academic or professional reasons, if there's space. At most 6 credits a term and 12 in total. Non-degree.

McGill students elsewhere need the Associate Dean's and instructor's permission and use a form. Other Quebec university students apply through BCI. Not for those seeking a law degree, recently refused, or meeting NCA requirements.
Mandatory B.C.L./J.D. courses, 600-level courses and two complementary courses are closed to Special Students.
878-application-deadlines-for-law-underg: Online from September 1. Identify your category, since deadlines differ. Late applications are never accepted, and incomplete ones are cancelled the day after the document deadline. Upload everything except references and some transcripts. First-year, Transfer and Advanced Standing start only in September.
879-first-year-fall: Application / documents: University, November 1 / November 8. Mature, November 1 / November 8. CEGEP and Baccalaureate, March 1 / March 7.
879-applicants-to-upper-years: Application / documents, Fall: Advanced Standing, November 1 / January 15. Transfer, May 1 / June 15. Comité des équivalences and Chambre des notaires, May 1 / July 1. Special, August 1 / August 8. Visiting (Fall or Winter), May 1 / June 15. Exchange, April 15 / May 1.
Winter: Exchange, September 15 / October 1. Comité and Chambre, October 1 / December 1. Special, December 1 / December 8.
879-application-supporting-documents: Everyone sends transcripts, a personal statement, a CV and references (not Exchange). Visiting and Exchange add a letter of permission or nomination; Comité applicants the final decision; Exchange a passport copy. LSAT scores come directly from LSAC.
Check your Portal checklist often. With over 1,300 applications a year, logging can take 48 hours near deadlines. Documents become McGill's property and aren't returned or forwarded.
879-uploading-supporting-documents: Upload, don't mail, and don't mail anything already uploaded. Only one version of the personal statement, Extenuating Circumstances form and CV is accepted, so check before uploading. To update transcripts, contact Admissions. Extra items are ignored.
879-mailing-supporting-documents: For documents that can't be uploaded: Law Admissions Office, New Chancellor Day Hall, Room 418, 3644 Peel St., H3A 1W9. Questions: 514-398-6602, admissions.law@mcgill.ca, mcgill.ca/law/bcl-jd.
880-transcripts: A full record of all post-secondary study, updated until a final decision. Quebec universities can send through BCI (ask your registrar), which counts as official. Everything else is uploaded and treated as unofficial until an offer depends on official copies, which come in a sealed envelope or to officialschooldocs@mcgill.ca directly from the school or a service like Parchment.
Scan in the original orientation. McGill may ask for official records at any time and rescind offers over discrepancies.

McGill transcripts are obtained for you, except grades from exchanges. Submit transcripts for exchange, visiting and independent study not on your home transcript. Other languages need a translation by the school or a certified translator.

CEGEP applicants give a Permanent Code, without which processing waits; records come from Quebec from mid-October. Quebec Baccalaureate needs official transcripts. Transfers send Winter results when available. LSDAS and OLSAS aren't used. Report language courses taken outside a degree, with proof.
880-personal-statement: 750 words of your own thinking: why law, why McGill, and what you'd bring. It also shows your writing and judgment in English or French. Members of equity-deserving groups are encouraged to explain how their circumstances and experience relate to studying law here. You don't need to plan on practising.
